title: Provision ALB Listener
scenario: Your platform team needs ALB Listener for accepting HTTP traffic on port 80. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_lb_listener.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).

focus.title: Complete the aws_lb_listener resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lb_listener.

hints.why: A load balancer is the stable entry point in front of changing compute. Listeners and target groups define how traffic reaches the application.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_lb_listener" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lb_listener. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a load balancer when traffic must be distributed, health-checked or terminated before reaching backend instances.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_lb_listener" "this"`. Use this code shape: port; protocol; load_balancer_arn; default_action { type; target_group_arn }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.lb_arn`, `aws_lb_target_group.this.arn`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
